\subsection*{Why the largest errors occur}
Fresh single-FET simulations at the recorded in-gate biases reconstruct each of the five worst gates' SPICE powers. The table attributes signed gate error to the dominant OFF-device group. Contributions are percentage points of whole-gate error; they include each group's leakage share.

OR2 00: the NOR output drives the output-inverter OFF PMOS gate below VDD. Across 200 corners this shortfall has median 1.31 mV and maximum 8.95 mV. Changing only that gate voltage back to VDD in fresh single-FET simulations shows that the shortfall raises its true power by a median 2.70\% and up to 17.17\%. The frozen model's median signed error is +0.05\% at the prescribed rail bias, but -2.76\% at the actual internal-node bias. OFF training fixes the gate at its prescribed rail; the learned OFF channel features omit gate-voltage variation. This explains the systematic underprediction, especially at hot corners.

INV 0 and NOR2 00 at corner 16: the OFF NMOS group supplies approximately 68.5\% of the gate leakage and is overpredicted by about 4.44\% per device, despite an exactly 0 V gate bias. This is a local regression outlier rather than the OR2 gate-bias mechanism. Only 4 of the 15,000 held-out NMOS OFF power predictions exceed 4.4\% error. This corner combines relatively thin NMOS oxide (lower 14.5\% of corners) with high VDD (upper 7\% of corners). The separate causal effect of those process parameters has not been isolated.

Complete parity checker: the worst row is input 01111111, corner 94 at 124.5 degrees C, with signed error -3.102\%. Relative to the same full-circuit SPICE reference, the frozen surrogate contributes -0.264 percentage points and replacing the connected circuit by standalone ideal-input gates contributes -2.837 percentage points. These contributions sum to the total error. Thus the prescribed ideal-input/no-loading hierarchy dominates this circuit outlier. This diagnostic uses existing gate and complete-circuit references only for evaluation; it does not change any ML prediction.
